samples.identification: ALMOFID 23.00.00 database reset installer, Setup Factory runtime
evidence: Rizin confirms the native extractor at 0x401484 locates the E0E0..E7E7 archive header at file offset 0x11e00. The setup engine begins at 0x11e22 and is 1390592 bytes. Code at 0x4017c8 XORs only the first 2000 bytes with 7, writes the engine, and the launcher runs it from its setup temporary directory.

Reproducing the header unmasking produces a valid UPX image. upx -d recovers a 3824640-byte setup engine, whose own error and restore-point wrappers were traced. The oledlg.dll dialog follows an actual failed system-directory LoadLibraryA at 0x41f00c; SRRemoveRestorePoint at 0x4548ae is a general runtime API wrapper, not evidence of recovery sabotage.

LZMA stream at 0x1b733e decompresses to 113026 bytes of complete installer configuration and scripts. It identifies ALMOFID 23.00.00, author Ahmed.BOUBAKRI, destination C:\ALMOFID, and two application members: AlmofidDLL.dll and DataBase.accdb.

The installer explicitly warns in French that this package resets the database and destroys student names, schooling, marks and archives. This disclosed reset operation agrees with the files it replaces. Pre/post install and uninstall hooks contain no custom execution; shutdown calls the standard reboot handler.

The DLL from LZMA offset 0x1ddf3b is a 37376-byte VB.NET library. dnfile/dncil inspection covers all methods and member references. AlmofidValidation has 7939 IL instructions and no calls; AlmofidValidationRotation uses Len/Mid/Asc/Chr/string concatenation. Remaining methods are VB.NET application/settings/resource/generic instance helpers. No network, process execution, payload loading or credential acquisition path was found.

The remaining application member starts at 0x1e15f2 with a Standard ACE DB header and encrypted Office database metadata. Configuration installs it as data and does not launch it. Images and the embedded Lua 5.1 runtime account for the other unpacked members.

Forager retrieved the supplied Triage report. Its score-10 custom signature is UPX dump on OEP; other reported packing, dropped-engine execution, DLL loading, locale and storage queries fit the installer. Forager could not resolve the configured publisher homepage www.almofidahmedboubakri.com.
samples.limitations: Publisher distribution and deployment context remain unverified. Encrypted Access contents cannot be independently audited without the password. Benign is the balance of the recovered program and disclosed purpose, not a conclusion from a clean scan.
samples.traits: No firing hostile/suspicious finding on the original, extracted Lua member, recovered engine or application DLL requires a correction. All original detections remain.

samples.identification: Screaming Radish.8466 DOS COM memory image
evidence: 8722-byte artifact has a zeroed 256-byte PSP prefix and an 8466-byte program starting at file/memory offset 0x100.

16-bit disassembly at 0x11c loads DX=0x21d5, binding the create target to the embedded c:\command.com string. CX=0 and AX=3c02 followed by INT 21h create/truncate the DOS command interpreter. AL=2 does not set file attributes.
AH=40h at 0x136 writes CX=0x2112 bytes from DS:0100h to the returned handle, then AH=3eh closes it. This replaces COMMAND.COM with the self image and destroys the old interpreter contents.
Repeated EB 01 90 branches skip NOP padding between saved registers and DOS operations. The later INT 10h AX=1110h installs a 256-character custom font block, retained as neutral graphics behavior.
samples.coverage_gap: Exactly one distinct hostile behavior, command-interpreter self-image overwrite, and one suspicious padding behavior are supported. A second hostile detection would duplicate that overwrite; font loading alone has no hostile intent claim.
samples.traits: Existing Cleave hostile overwrite, suspicious skipped-NOP pattern, and notable file/font traits already describe the supported behavior accurately; no DOS YAML changed.

samples.identification: Shipping-label LNK/VBScript remote-code loader in fixed VHD/NTFS
evidence: 7z independently lists a fixed Windows VHD with NTFS label A. Application members are parcel_shipping_label.lnk and logo/receipt.vbs; remaining entries are ordinary filesystem metadata.

Cleave LNK facts and the extracted binary show D:\logo\receipt.vbs as the target, .\logo\receipt.vbs as the relative target, D:\logo as the working directory, and SHELL32.dll icon index 324. Opening the shipping-labelled shortcut activates the VBS through its registered handler.

Decoded UTF-16 VBS assigns character codes 97..122 to variables, then interleaves empty literals and those variables to reconstruct https://paste.ee/d/tmxzk. This hides the endpoint rather than reconstructing the subsequently evaluated script body.

The top-level code creates MSXML2.XMLHTTP, calls an open wrapper with GET, reconstructed URL and False (synchronous), calls a send wrapper, assigns responseText to treu and passes that same variable to sabacuim. That helper executes its parameter with ExecuteGlobal under On Error Resume Next. The response-to-evaluator path is established by tracing the caller and helper parameters, not by the loose rule co-occurrences.

Forager fetch of the reconstructed URL returns 404. The final payload cannot be identified, but the concealed remote-source execution chain and document-themed shortcut support malicious intent independently of payload recovery.
samples.missing_context: No authorized deployment or legitimate business application was established. No credential-stealer, ransomware or named malware-family attribution is supported by this artifact.
samples.traits: Two distinct suspicious findings remain on the script: variable ExecuteGlobal evaluation and redundant empty-literal concatenation. Three unbound hostile co-occurrence composites are removed; all underlying network, character-construction and evaluation facts remain. The LNK working-directory observation is relocated and corrected without changing its matcher.
samples.coverage_gap: Static analysis proves hostile remote code activation. Current VBS facts expose neither a flow graph nor bindings, so the loose composites do not justify an automatic source-to-sink assertion. Suspicious coverage is kept; no duplicate hostile proxy was added.

removed_hostile_composites.chr-built-vbs-execute-loader: Dense Chr construction plus an evaluation statement does not show that constructed characters become evaluated code. The actual sample constructs a URL; a local-code/character-label control also matched. Retained primitives separately report both capabilities.
removed_hostile_composites.chr-built-vbs-executeglobal-loader: Same unsupported data-flow claim, with a global evaluator. The real URL-construction path refutes the advertised reconstructed-payload relationship. Both constituent traits remain.
removed_hostile_composites.vbs-remote-response-executeglobal: HTTP client/body references within 4096 bytes of ExecuteGlobal do not bind the response to the evaluator. The disconnected-response/local-code control matched the old hostile. The actual sample is manually confirmed malicious via helper-parameter tracing; generic references remain detected.

relocation.reason: The unchanged matcher proves a short D-Z drive working-directory value, not a builder, staging operation, non-system drive or C2 role. Criticality stays notable.
relocation.consumer: objectives/execution/lure/document::lnk-lure-named-staged-payload references the relocated observation; a modified document-executable shortcut still fires it.

corrections.added: objectives/anti-static/obfuscation/string/junking::vbs-interleaved-empty-literal-concat detects four redundant empty strings interleaved with variable concatenation at an assignment. It is suspicious concealment, not payload execution.
corrections.consumer_audit: No exact or execution-ancestor YAML consumers select the three removed composites. LNK exact consumer was rewired. The broader C2 selector in the native hosts-sinkhole composite is PE/DLL-only; the CrystalX broader C2 exclusion requires unrelated family evidence absent here. Constituent matchers, severities and scope were retained. No broad replacement or score-padding aliases were introduced.

controls.new_padding: Positive standalone VBS and real UTF-16 loader match; ordinary concatenation, comments and unrelated evaluation fail.
controls.lnk: Original D:\logo matches the relocated notable observation; C:\logo fails. A document-executable mutation retains lnk-lure-named-staged-payload. Existing ordinary shortcut control remains unflagged.
controls.retained_attack_fixtures: testdata/hostile/wsh-chr-wrapper-response-exec.vbs retains wsh-xmlhttp-response-execute-downloader and wrapped-chr-vbs-executeglobal-loader; testdata/hostile/vbs-numeric-table-execute-loader.vbs retains split-decoded-vbs-execute-stage and arithmetic-decoded-vbs-execute-loader.
controls.retained_atoms: Dense Chr construction, XMLHTTP client/body and variable evaluator observations survive the corrections. The actual original PE and embedded Lua findings are identical; DOS findings are identical.

classifier_disagreements: Atomscan 2.13.0 labels all three original files BENIGN before and after. DOS and VHD are unknown to this bundled analyzer; standalone Cleave identifies dos_com/vhd and recursively analyzes the VHD members. This is a format/analyzer integration miss, not a YAML evidence gap.

The extracted VBS remains ML hostile (vbs route cls=2, probability 0.99915206 -> 0.9989665); the shortcut remains benign. The corrected VBS has two suspicious observations rather than three unsupported hostile composite labels.

The benign installer retains probability 0.95646256 with an emitted benign decision. v18 model/v19 extractor compatibility warnings make raw probabilities and emitted decisions distinct; neither determines the analyst verdict.
verification.material_detection_losses: Three hostile co-occurrence labels disappear from the VHD member and aggregated parent. Their underlying observations are retained. These changes expose a need for VBS source-to-evaluator flow support. No other original attack evidence is lost.
